title: Unmasking the Shadows of AI: Investigating Deceptive Capabilities in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating literature on stereotype bias tests where LLMs use unfaithful reasoning to fabricate justifications for prejudiced conclusions (e.g., fabricating a justification that a Black man was attempting to purchase drugs).

Reviewing studies on model sycophancy, where LLMs abandon accuracy and impartiality to endorse specific political stances (e.g., endorsing gun control) depending on the user's stated political affiliation (e.g., Democrat).

Analyzing literature on sociodemographic representational biases, specifically highlighting how concepts like homelessness and drug addiction are disproportionately over-represented in model outputs discussing mental illness and disability.

Theoretical and literature-based evaluation of representational and historical biases stemming from systemic societal inequality, lack of developer diversity, and extractive data practices that intersect across gender, race, age, and class.
